title: TimeMaster: Training Time-Series Multimodal LLMs to Reason via Reinforcement Learning
methods: Qwen2.5-VL-3B on plotted time series; SFT (~1k GPT-4o samples per dataset) then token-level GRPO (G=5, eps=0.2, beta=0.001).
findings: Reward r = 0.1*r_fmt + 0.9*1[c_hat=c*] (+ soft reward = correct-conditioned mean of four GPT-4o judged scores; weight 0 in main table).
TimerBed ECG 43,673 samples/4 classes; EMG 205 samples/3 classes. ECG accuracy 60.00% vs 43.75% for few-shot VL-Time; EMG 100%.
Trained on 4xA100-80GB or RTX A6000 48GB.
limitations: Classification only; ECG/EMG are two of six tasks; small EMG set.

title: OpenTSLM: Time-Series Language Models for Reasoning over Multivariate Medical Text- and Time-Series Data
methods: SoftPrompt and Flamingo TSLMs on Llama-3.2-1B/3B and Gemma-3; curriculum SFT with LoRA; no RL.
findings: Datasets: TSQA, M4 captions, HAR-CoT (DaLiAc, DOMINO, HHAR, PAMAP2, RealWorld), Sleep-CoT (SleepEDF), ECG-QA-CoT (PTB-XL based ECG-QA).
Sleep F1 69.88 (SoftPrompt-1B) vs 9.05 tokenized fine-tuned and 15.47 GPT-4o; Flamingo-3B ~60GB for five 10k-length series.
limitations: SFT only; CoT labels generated by GPT-4o.

title: ECG-R1: Protocol-Guided and Modality-Agnostic MLLM for Reliable ECG Interpretation
methods: Qwen3-VL-8B + ECG-CoCa signal encoder; protocol-guided CoT SFT, interleaved modality dropout, then DAPO (eps_low 0.2, eps_high 0.3) on 3,948 RL samples.
findings: R_total = R_format + R_accuracy(Jaccard of diagnosis sets) + lambda*R_EDER; per-step evidence coverage r_step = |match(E_k(y), y_k)|/|E_k(y)|, evidence phrases extracted by DeepSeek-V3.1.
Train: 30k MIMIC-IV-ECG protocol CoT + ECGInstruct; test: ECG-Grounding 2,381. Diagnosis accuracy 80.29 vs GEM 74.70.
limitations: Evidence extraction relies on another LLM; compute not disclosed.

title: MedTVT-R1: A Multimodal LLM Empowering Medical Reasoning and Diagnosis
methods: LLaMA-3.2-1B + LoRA (r=8) with ECGFM-KED, ViT-B/16 and Symile encoders; PT -> SFT -> GRPO (G=8, 500 iterations).
findings: R = R_format + R_Jaccard over predicted vs true disease sets.
MedTVT-QA: 8,706 ECG+CXR+lab combinations (8,331 train/375 test) from MIMIC-IV, MIMIC-IV-ECG, MIMIC-CXR-JPG; 7 disease groups incl. sepsis and pneumonia.
F1 0.519; removing RFT lowers F1 to 0.499. Trained on 8xA800-80GB.
limitations: Instruction data generated by GPT-4o; baselines are general MLLMs without ECG training.

title: EHR-R1: A Reasoning-Enhanced Foundational Language Model for Electronic Health Record Analysis
methods: Qwen3-1.7B/8B and Qwen2.5-72B; domain adaptation, thinking-graph reasoning SFT, GRPO limited to 500 examples per task.
findings: R = R_fmt + R_acc with R_acc = ACC for decision-making tasks and F1 for risk-prediction tasks (lambda=1).
EHR-Ins: 300k reasoning + 3.5M non-reasoning cases over 42 tasks from MIMIC-IV; EHR-Bench 21k test samples (24 decision + 18 risk tasks, 24h history window); also MIMIC-IV-CDM and EHRSHOT.
EHR-Bench risk AUROC 0.952 (72B); EHRSHOT 128-shot 1.7B 0.747 vs 0.600 for base.
limitations: 72B GRPO used 128 GPUs; benchmark built by the same authors from MIMIC-IV.

title: Training LLMs for EHR-Based Reasoning Tasks via Reinforcement Learning
methods: EHRMind: lightweight SFT warm-up then RLVR with GRPO on Llama-3-3B (k=12 rollouts, lr 1e-6, KL 0.001).
findings: Rewards are exact match / classification accuracy on MedCalc-Bench, TREC 2021 Clinical Trials and EHRSHOT diagnosis.
2xA100-80GB with FSDP and offloading. MedCalc 51.96% vs 48.13% DeepSeek-R1.
limitations: MedCalc and trial matching are not time series; only EHRSHOT is longitudinal.

title: Toward Better EHR Reasoning in LLMs: Reinforcement Learning with Expert Attention Guidance
methods: EAG-RL: expert-guided MCTS trajectories for SFT, then GRPO-style RL with entropy-adaptive clipping; Qwen2.5-3B/7B, Llama3.1-8B; expert model Concare.
findings: R = 0.6*R_cls + 0.4*R_att; R_cls = log(y*p + (1-y)(1-p)) + Delta, Delta = beta(p-0.5) for correct positives and beta(0.5-p) for correct negatives; R_att = Jaccard(model-cited features, expert-highlighted features).
MIMIC-IV mortality/30-day readmission (train 8,750, test 200; mortality 8.5%) and TJH (train 140, test 200).
Qwen2.5-7B MIMIC-IV mortality AUROC 77.21 / AUPRC 23.99 vs 53.90 / 10.68 vanilla. 4 GPUs with 48GB.
limitations: Test set of 200 patients with 17 deaths; beta unspecified; baselines are mostly LLMs.

title: Agentifying Patient Dynamics within LLMs through Interacting with Clinical World Model
methods: SepsisAgent: Qwen3-4B-Instruct; patient-dynamics SFT, propose-simulate-refine behaviour cloning, GRPO inside a GRU clinical world model.
findings: R(tau) = R_out(s_T) + sum r(s_t,s_t+1) - lambda_g*P_g(tau), r = C0*1(dSOFA=0 and SOFA>0) + C1*dSOFA + C2*dLactate (Raghu form) with a guideline-violation penalty.
MIMIC-IV sepsis 20,092 ICU stays, 4h steps, 42 state variables, 5x5 fluid x vasopressor actions.
DR 10.01 vs clinicians 5.06; unsafe actions 0.22% vs 0.54% (offline estimates).
limitations: All evaluation is off-policy or world-model based.

title: Large language model-augmented offline reinforcement learning framework for sepsis management in critical care (MORE-CLEAR)
methods: CQL (alpha=2) with dueling DQN on structured ICU data plus LLM-summarised clinical notes (Gemma-3-27B summaries; frozen Llama-3.1-8B/BERT/ClinicalBERT embeddings; gated fusion and cross-modal attention).
findings: Reward +1 for 90-day survival, -1 otherwise, 0 at intermediate steps; gamma=0.98; 4h steps; 5x5 actions.
MIMIC-III 11,114, MIMIC-IV 10,203 and SNUH 599 sepsis patients; baselines BCQ, CQL, text-only and multimodal variants; OPE with OPERA, DR, FQE, WIS and BDESR.
limitations: Offline estimates only; SNUH data private.

title: GEM: Empowering MLLM for Grounded ECG Understanding with Time Series and Images
methods: Dual-encoder ECG MLLM over signals and 12-lead images; ECG-Grounding data and grounded ECG understanding benchmark.
findings: Reported gains of 7.4% (CSN), 22.7% explainability and 24.8% grounding. Used as the SOTA baseline by ECG-R1.
limitations: Abstract-level; training type not confirmed on the inspected page.

title: Teach Multimodal LLMs to Comprehend Electrocardiographic Images
methods: PULSE: instruction-tuned MLLM on ECGInstruct (>1M samples); ECGBench with four tasks over nine datasets.
findings: 15-30% average accuracy improvement over general MLLMs; used as baseline by ECG-R1.

title: ECG-QA: A Comprehensive Question Answering Dataset Combined With Electrocardiogram
methods: ECG question answering dataset with 70 question templates, including comparison questions over two ECGs.
findings: Source of OpenTSLM ECG-QA-CoT (PTB-XL based).

title: HEARTS: Benchmarking LLM Reasoning on Health Time Series
methods: Benchmark of 16 datasets, 12 health domains, 20 signal modalities, 110 tasks; 16 LLMs evaluated.
findings: LLMs substantially underperform specialised models; performance weakly related to general reasoning scores.
limitations: Abstract-level; dataset names not listed on inspected page.

title: RealICU: Do LLM Agents Understand Long-Context ICU Data? A Benchmark Beyond Behavior Imitation
methods: MIMIC-IV long-context ICU benchmark with hindsight physician annotations (Gold: 930 windows from 94 patients; Scale: 11,862 windows).
findings: LLMs show a recall-safety trade-off and anchoring bias; no RL training.

title: TRIAGE: Dialectical Reasoning for Explainable Risk Prediction on Irregularly Sampled Medical Time Series with LLMs
methods: LLM generates outcome-specific rationales over competing outcomes for ISMTS risk prediction.
findings: Addresses risk polarization; 81% calibration error reduction and +3.3% AUPRC reported.

title: Rethinking Large Language Models For Irregular Time Series Classification In Critical Care
methods: Benchmark of LLM-based vs irregular-TS models on PhysioNet 2012 (11,988), MIMIC-III (24,681) and semi-synthetic MIT-BIH AF.
findings: Baselines: mTAND, Warpformer, Time-LLM, S2IP-LLM, CALF, FSCA, MOMENT, UniTS.
Encoder design matters more than alignment strategy; LLM methods need >=10x training time for comparable results; Warpformer wins in few-shot.

title: Yet Another ICU Benchmark: A Flexible Multi-Center Framework for Clinical ML
methods: YAIB: cohort, preprocessing and training framework over MIMIC-III/IV, eICU, HiRID and AmsterdamUMCdb.
findings: Tasks: ICU mortality (24h), AKI and sepsis onset (hourly), kidney function, LoS.
Baselines: LR, Elastic Net, LightGBM, GRU, LSTM, TCN, Transformer.
Dataset, cohort definition and preprocessing affect performance more than model class.

title: Early Prediction of Sepsis from Clinical Data: The PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2019
methods: Challenge dataset (40,336 patients, three hospital systems, 40 hourly variables) with a clinical utility score.
findings: Utility constants from official code: dt_early=-12h, dt_optimal=-6h, dt_late=+3h, max_u_tp=1, min_u_fn=-2, u_fp=-0.05, u_tn=0; normalised (U - U_inaction)/(U_optimal - U_inaction).
limitations: A scoring rule for evaluation, not an RL paper.

title: Adaptive-Halting Policy Network for Early Classification
methods: EARLIEST: RNN discriminator plus RL controller deciding when to halt and classify.
findings: Jointly optimises accuracy and earliness with a user-controlled trade-off.

title: Stop&Hop: Early Classification of Irregular Time Series
methods: GRU-D prefix encoder, classifier, and REINFORCE halting policy that can hop forward in continuous time.
findings: Reward +1 for a correct prediction and -1 otherwise at stop; waiting probabilities penalised with a tunable weight.
PhysioNet 2012 mortality (4,000 patients, 42 variables, 13.8% positive) plus ExtraSensory.

title: An Optimal Policy for Patient Laboratory Tests in Intensive Care Units
methods: Pareto-optimal fitted-Q iteration for lab ordering in MIMIC-III.
findings: Vector reward r_t = [r_SOFA, r_treat, r_info, -r_cost]: SOFA change, treatment-onset indicator, forecast information gain, and an exponentially decaying lab cost.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Sepsis Treatment
methods: Dueling double DQN on MIMIC-III Sepsis-3 cohort, 4h steps, 5x5 fluid x vasopressor actions.
findings: r = C0*1(SOFA_t+1 = SOFA_t and SOFA_t+1 > 0) + C1*(SOFA_t+1 - SOFA_t) + C2*tanh(Lact_t+1 - Lact_t), C0=-0.025, C1=-0.125, C2=-2; terminal +/-15.

title: Continuous State-Space Models for Optimal Sepsis Treatment - a Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
methods: Dueling double DQN with prioritized replay; doubly robust OPE.
findings: Terminal-only reward Rmax=15; MIMIC-III v1.4 Sepsis-3 cohort of 15,583 survivors and 2,315 non-survivors; test set 3,580.

title: The Artificial Intelligence Clinician learns optimal treatment strategies for sepsis in intensive care
methods: Policy iteration on a discretised MDP learned from ICU data; independent validation cohort.
findings: Terminal reward +/-100 for 90-day survival (via secondary sources); validation mortality lowest where clinician doses matched AI.
limitations: Main text not opened in this round; cohort sizes not written.

title: Optimal medication dosing from suboptimal clinical examples: a deep reinforcement learning approach
methods: DHMM state estimation + Q-network for heparin dosing, MIMIC-II (4,470 patients).
findings: r_t = 2/(1+exp(-(aPTT_t-60))) - 2/(1+exp(-(aPTT_t-100))) - 1; maximal 1 inside the 60-100 s therapeutic window.
limitations: Formula taken from the survey S066, not the original IEEE paper.

title: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to Weaning of Mechanical Ventilation in Intensive Care Units
methods: Fitted-Q iteration with extremely randomized trees on MIMIC-III ventilation episodes.
findings: Reward combines threshold functions keeping vitals within range, a penalty for abrupt vital changes above 0.2, and terms for successful extubation or failed SBT/reintubation (constants C1-C7).

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Closed-Loop Blood Glucose Control
methods: SAC with recurrent networks on the UVA/Padova simulator.
findings: Reward = -Magni risk(b) = -10*(c0*log(b)^c1 - c2)^2, with -1e5 for BG outside 10-1,000 mg/dL; time-in-range and target-distance rewards performed worse.

title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Safer Blood Glucose Control in People with Type 1 Diabetes
methods: BCQ, CQL and TD3-BC vs PID and SAC-RNN on 30 UVA/Padova virtual patients.
findings: risk(g) = 10*(3.5506*log(g)^0.8353 - 3.7932)^2, reward = -risk, -1e5 outside 10-1,000 mg/dL. TIR 61.6% -> 65.3% for TD3-BC without more hypoglycaemia.

title: Towards Safe Mechanical Ventilation Treatment Using Deep Offline Reinforcement Learning
methods: DeepVent: CQL on MIMIC-III ventilation; action = 7x7x7 (tidal volume, FiO2, PEEP).
findings: Terminal +1/-1 for 90-day survival plus intermediate reward = normalised change of a modified APACHE II score (FiO2, RR and haematocrit removed).

title: Reinforcement Learning Assisted Oxygen Therapy for COVID-19 Patients Under Intensive Care
methods: DDPG for continuous oxygen flow (0-60 L/min) in 1,372 critically ill COVID-19 patients at NYU Langone.
findings: Terminal +15 survival / -15 death; estimated mortality 7.94% -> 5.37%.
limitations: Private cohort; estimated, not trial, mortality.

title: ICU-Sepsis: A Benchmark MDP Built from Real Medical Data
methods: Tabular MDP (716 states, 25 actions) from ~17,000 MIMIC-III sepsis patients following Komorowski et al.
findings: Reward +1 on transition to survival, 0 otherwise; random 0.78, clinician 0.78, optimal 0.88; DQN/PPO 0.86.
limitations: Benchmark only; authors warn against clinical conclusions.

title: DTR-Bench: An in silico Environment and Benchmark Platform for Reinforcement Learning Based Dynamic Treatment Regime
methods: Four simulators (chemotherapy, radio-chemotherapy, Oberst sepsis, SimGlucose) with PK/PD variance, noise and missingness.
findings: SimGlucose reward = risk term + glucose-change penalty + +/-100 terminal; Oberst sepsis +1 discharge/-1 death.
Algorithms: DQN, DDQN, dueling DDQN, C51, discrete SAC, recurrent variants, DDPG, TD3, SAC.

title: A Unified Benchmark for Dynamic Medical Treatment Reinforcement Learning (MedGym)
methods: Continuous-time sepsis environment fitted to MIMIC-III with physics-informed neural networks.
findings: Reward r = -SOFA - lambda*vasopressor; baselines SAC, PPO, TRPO, PPO-Lag, TRPO-Lag, DQN, CQL, Guarded CQL, TACOS.
SOFA reduction does not guarantee lactate-based safety; adaptive timing helps.

title: Are Large Language Models Dynamic Treatment Planners? An In Silico Study from a Prior Knowledge Injection Angle
methods: Zero-shot Qwen2.5 and Llama3 (1B-70B) vs DQN/PPO for insulin dosing in SimGlucose.
findings: LBGI/HBGI risk reward scaled to [-100, 0]. Qwen2.5-7B/14B/32B reach 62.8/62.1/62.3% normalised return; CoT made small models dose aggressively; no gain from 7B to 70B.
limitations: Simulation; zero-shot LLMs, no RL fine-tuning.

title: Exploring Time-Step Size in Reinforcement Learning for Sepsis Treatment
methods: Offline RL pipeline comparing 1, 2, 4 and 8 h steps.
findings: 1-2 h steps with a static behaviour policy gave the best performance and stability, challenging the 4 h convention.

title: Eliciting Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Time Series Analysis using Reinforcement Learning
methods: COUNTS: RVQ-VAE time-series tokens + SFT + GRPO on verifiable problems.
findings: Mentions medical diagnosis among target domains.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Clinical Decision Support: A Brief Survey
methods: Survey of DRL in clinical decision support.
findings: Reproduces the Nemati 2016 heparin reward formula and cohort description.
